description: University of California Irvine researchers publish FloodRISE hazard maps for Newport Bay and the Tijuana River Estuary. Zenodo lists thirty-six GeoTIFF rasters free under CC0. Layers include flood depth, duration, chance, force, shear stress and road blockage under historical events, king tides, rainfall, sea walls, dredging and 2035 or 2050 scenarios. The project describes a collaborative modelling process with local users. These rasters can drive flood exposure and road-access simulations in the two coastal study areas. No related catalogue record explicitly covers this scenario collection. Coverage is site-specific and scenario-specific, not measured continuous flooding or a region-wide forecast. File names identify interventions but do not establish probabilities for every layer; mixed assumptions need checking before comparison. No raster was downloaded or modelled depth validated.
name: Flood Resilient Infrastructure and Sustainable Environments (FloodRISE) data
notes: G6 item G6-1567. Metadata-only draft. Simulation-use and type tags are reviewer classifications. File contents and software execution were not checked. Unknown maturity does not assert active maintenance.
